doc.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: A repertoire of 150 arrangements and about 20 hits
summary: He gets bored quickly, travelled with 150-175 pieces and 16-20 recognizable hits.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: As many as we could do. I would get . . . My threshold for boredom is very high . . . very low, rather. I get bored very quickly. So we’d play a piece, and play it and play it, and I’d want to get a change. We ended up with a book of about—what we travelled with—a book of around 150, 175 pieces, out of which 16 to 20 were hits, where the audience would know that was this band. It was like you went into a gallery, and you look across the room and see Gauguin, Van Gogh, Matisse, Monet. You’ll know them. You don’t have to go and read them, if you know anything about . . . Anybody who knew anything about jazz would know what those pieces were. They would know it was the Artie Shaw Orchestra. So that was that.
